newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-LENTINI ON THE COMEBACK TRAIL, ALL THE WAY TO MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LENTINI ON THE COMEBACK TRAIL, ALL THE WAY TO MILAN.

text.p: Gigi Lentini, once the world's most expensive soccer player, may well have turned the corner on Sunday after spending three years in the doldrums following an horrific car accident.
Playing for Atalanta against his old club AC Milan, Lentini made a 40-metre break reminiscent of his best form to set up Filippo Inzaghi's goal in his side's 1-1 draw in Milan.
Later on Sunday, Lentini received another morale boost with an unexpected call-up from Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi for Wednesday's friendly against Bosnia in Sarajevo.
Lentini, 27, made international headlines in July 1992 when Milan splashed out a reported $14 million to buy him from Torino.

Almost exactly one year later, however, his career suffered a serious setback when he came close to death in a car accident on the Genoa-Turin motorway while driving home after playing for Milan in a friendly in Genoa.
Lentini took many months to recover from an accident in which he had suffered head injuries that left him in a coma for 24 hours.
For seasons Lentini was effectively relegated to the role of reserve at Milan, playing only 26 out of 68 league games, often as a substitute.
Keen to play regular first team soccer, Lentini accepted a close-season move on loan to Atalanta, a side coached by Emiliano Mondonico who worked with him at Torino.
On his return to the San Siro on Sunday, he was greeted with applause from his ex-fans and a banner which read, "Gigi Come Back To Us".

Speaking after the game, Lentini said he appreciated the reception by the Milan fans, adding: "We've got to keep playing with this spirit. As for Milan, they didn't look too good to me. You can see that it's not going to be their year."
Lentini's good form has already prompted speculation that Milan may want him back at the end of the season.
"I think I will be coming back and I would like to, but I'll be coming back with a different attitude," said Lentini.
Just as his club career suffered a dramatic turn around following his car accident, so too did Lentini's international career.
If Lentini plays in this week's match against Bosnia, it will be his 13th cap and his first since Italy's 1-0 World Cup qualifying defeat to Switzerland in May 1993.
